title: Three 1v1 Moves
subtitle: Three unnamed moves from one “3 crazy skills” clip, broken down with the 3D body reconstructed from it.
sourceNote: one public skills clip (credit its creator before any real use), the body motion reconstructed from it, and measurements taken from that motion.

skills.name: Drag, spin and go
skills.intro: He drags the ball across the defender, spins back round it with his body in the way, and takes it off the other side. It looks like a roulette-style turn, but the video doesn’t name it.

notice.title: Receive
notice.text: The ball arrives at his feet with the defender closing.

notice.title: Drag across
notice.text: A long stride drags the ball across the defender.

notice.title: Spin back
notice.text: He turns back round the ball, his body between it and the defender.

notice.title: Go
notice.text: Out the other side, away from the defender’s reach.

skills.adds: Watch the ball foot stay on the ball through the spin; use Behind to see where the defender would be.
unsure: The move’s name: the video only numbers it.
Turn angles: the camera pans to follow him, so the 3D’s turning is mixed with the camera’s.
Which part of the foot drags the ball: it happens behind his body.

phases.name: Shuffle in
phases.video: He shuffles sideways, waiting for the ball and watching the defender.
phases.shows: His body bobs as he shuffles; the ball isn’t at his feet yet.
phases.why: Clear view; no ball contact to measure yet.

phases.name: Receive and drag
phases.cue: Take it across the defender with a long stride.
phases.video: He takes the ball and drags it across in front of the defender with a long stride.
phases.shows: The ball foot comes into contact at about 1.08 s and his body drops about 23 cm into the stride.
phases.why: Fast movement; touches are counted within a few centimetres.

phases.name: Spin back
phases.cue: Turn back round the ball; keep your body in the way.
phases.video: He spins back round the ball and briefly faces the camera, ball shielded from the defender.
phases.shows: 3 touches as he comes round, the foot within about 1 cm of the ball, body still about 17 cm low.
phases.why: The ball is close to both feet here; which foot touches is the 3D’s best guess.

phases.name: Go past
phases.cue: Push it out the other side and accelerate.
phases.video: He comes out on the other side and runs past the defender.
phases.shows: The body rises back to upright as he accelerates away from the camera.
phases.why: Running away from one camera; depth is rough.

drills.title: Drag across a cone
drills.how: Ball in front of a cone. Drag it sideways across the cone with the sole of one foot in a long stride.
checks: The ball stayed under my sole
My stride was long and low
I stayed balanced at the end

drills.title: Drag and spin
drills.how: After the drag, turn back round the ball so your back faces the cone, then take it out the other side.
checks: My back was to the cone during the turn
The ball never left my feet
I came out on the other side

drills.title: At jogging pace
drills.how: Jog in and do the whole move without stopping.
checks: No stop between the drag and the spin
I accelerated out of it
I kept the ball close

drills.title: Against a passive defender
drills.how: Drag it across a partner, spin back as they follow it, and go the other way.
checks: They followed the drag
My body blocked them during the spin
I got past on the other side

challenges.title: Where is his body?
challenges.prompt: Frozen mid-spin. Why is his back towards the defender?
options: It keeps his body between the ball and the defender
challenges.explain: Turning his back shields the ball while he changes direction.

challenges.title: Spot the drag
challenges.prompt: Tap when he drags the ball across the defender.
challenges.label: Drag!
challenges.explain: The long stride across the defender comes just after he receives it.

skills.name: Feint and burst
skills.intro: Face up to the defender with the ball between your feet, sell a move one way with your leg and body, then take it the other way and sprint past.

notice.title: Square up
notice.text: Ball between his feet, facing the defender.

notice.title: Sell it
notice.text: His leg swings out as if he’s going one way.

notice.title: Other way
notice.text: He takes it the other way.

notice.title: Burst
notice.text: He’s past the defender’s side before they can recover.

skills.adds: Use Behind to see the feint the way the defender sees it.
unsure: The move’s name: the video only numbers it.
Turn angles: the camera pans to follow him, so the 3D’s turning is mixed with the camera’s.
Whether the feint foot touches the ball: the foot passes very close to it.

phases.name: Square up
phases.cue: Ball between your feet; make them wait.
phases.video: He stands facing the defender with the ball between his feet.
phases.shows: His feet are planted at 3.05 s and his body is upright: about 1 cm lower at most.

phases.name: Sell it
phases.cue: Swing a leg out; lean that way.
phases.video: His leg swings out and his body leans as if he’s going that way.
phases.shows: The ball foot lifts and swings round the ball while his weight stays over the standing foot, ready to push off.
phases.why: Weight is inferred from where the body sits between the feet.

phases.name: Other way
phases.cue: Take it the opposite way with your next touch.
phases.video: The next touch takes the ball the other way.
phases.shows: 3 touches around 3.8–4.0 s move the ball the opposite way to the feint.
phases.why: The ball is close to both feet; which foot touches is the 3D’s best guess.

phases.name: Burst past
phases.video: He pushes the ball ahead and sprints past the defender.
phases.shows: He drops about 19 cm into the first sprint steps; the ball runs more than a metre ahead.
phases.why: Running away from the camera; depth is rough.

drills.title: The feint alone
drills.how: Facing a cone, swing one leg out and lean that way, then push off the other way. Make the lean big.
checks: My shoulders leaned with the feint
I pushed off the other way
I stayed low

drills.title: Feint with the ball
drills.how: Ball between your feet. Feint one way, then take it the other way with the outside or inside of your foot.
checks: The feint didn’t touch the ball
My next touch went the other way
The ball stayed close

drills.title: Feint and sprint
drills.how: Add a five-metre sprint after the touch.
checks: I sprinted straight after the touch
I pushed the ball into space
I didn’t look down

drills.title: Against a passive defender
drills.how: Face a partner a metre away. Feint, take it the other way and get past them.
checks: They moved with the feint
I went the other way quickly
I got past before they recovered

challenges.title: What comes next?
challenges.prompt: Frozen mid-feint. Predict his next touch.
options: He takes it the opposite way to the feint
He goes the way he’s leaning
challenges.explain: The feint sells one direction; the touch goes the other.

challenges.title: Spot the touch
challenges.prompt: Tap the touch that takes the ball the other way.
challenges.label: Touch!
challenges.explain: The touch comes straight after the leg swing.

skills.name: Stop and cut back
skills.intro: He carries the ball across the defender, stops it dead under his foot as they follow, and cuts back the other way into space.

notice.title: Carry across
notice.text: He runs across the defender’s front with the ball.

notice.title: Stop
notice.text: Foot on the ball; it stops dead.

notice.title: Cut back
notice.text: He takes it back the way he came.

notice.title: Away
notice.text: A long stride into the space behind the defender.

skills.adds: Use the top view to see the sharp change of direction in the paths.
unsure: The move’s name: the video only numbers it.
Turn angles: the camera pans to follow him, so the 3D’s turning is mixed with the camera’s.
Whether it’s the sole or the inside of the foot that stops the ball.

phases.name: Carry across
phases.cue: Run across the defender; make them follow.
phases.video: He dribbles across the defender’s front, side-on to them.
phases.shows: His body sits about 26 cm lower than standing as he carries the ball across.
phases.why: Clear view; the camera pans with him.

phases.name: Stop it
phases.cue: Foot on the ball; stop it dead.
phases.video: He puts his foot on the ball and stops it as the defender keeps going.
phases.shows: 2 touches in under half a second, the foot within about 1 cm of the ball.
phases.why: Touches counted within a few centimetres; ball depth is estimated.

phases.name: Cut back
phases.cue: Take it back the way you came.
phases.video: He drags it back and turns into the space he came from.
phases.shows: 5 quick touches take the ball back the other way.
phases.why: Fast touches; the camera swings round with him.

phases.name: Away
phases.video: He strides away from the defender with the ball ahead.
phases.shows: His body rises back to upright as he accelerates.
phases.why: Fast running with a moving camera.

drills.title: Stop it dead
drills.how: Dribble along a line and stop the ball dead under your sole on a call.
checks: The ball stopped dead
My body stopped with it
I kept my balance

drills.title: Stop and cut back
drills.how: Stop it, then drag it back and go the way you came.
checks: I went straight back the other way
I didn’t lose the ball on the turn
I accelerated out of it

drills.title: Across a defender
drills.how: Dribble across a cone, stop and cut back behind it.
checks: I ran across the cone’s front
I stopped beside it
I cut back behind it

drills.title: Against a following defender
drills.how: Let a partner follow you across, then stop and cut back as they commit.
checks: They kept running when I stopped
I cut back into space
I got clear before they turned

challenges.title: Spot the stop
challenges.prompt: Tap when he stops the ball dead.
challenges.label: Stop!
challenges.explain: His foot comes onto the ball as the defender follows.

challenges.title: What next?
challenges.prompt: Frozen as he stops the ball. Predict his next move.
options: Cut back the way he came
challenges.explain: Stopping the ball while the defender keeps running opens the space behind him.

limits: The camera follows him by hand, so turn angles aren’t shown and paths include the camera’s own movement.
None of the three moves is named in the video; the names here describe what he does.
tests: Whether descriptive names (“Feint and burst”) help or confuse learners who know the moves by other names.
